nodes.title: Markup that carries the spec's class names
nodes.why: A design review compares named parts; the checks read the same names. Building the structure first means every CSS rule after it has a target.
nodes.alternative: Style by element and nesting, such as `main > section:first-child`.
nodes.tradeoff: Structural selectors break as soon as the markup moves, and nobody reading the CSS can tell which part of the design a rule implements.

nodes.title: One breakpoint on the screen grid
nodes.why: The spec has one breakpoint, so one media query on `.events-screen` switches the layout; the preview and the panel stay in the same order at every width.
nodes.alternative: Use flexbox with `flex-wrap` and fixed widths.
nodes.tradeoff: Wrapping flexbox stacks at whatever width the content forces, not at 900 px, so the layout would not match the spec at in-between widths.

nodes.title: Format in the building's time zone

anchor.snippet: const timeFormat = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: TIME_ZONE, hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit', hour12: true });

nodes.why: The building is in New York, so two of the events fall on the previous evening there. One formatter with `timeZone` gives the local time whatever zone the browser is in.
nodes.alternative: Shift the UTC hour by a fixed offset.
nodes.tradeoff: A fixed offset is wrong for half the year, because daylight saving time changes it.

nodes.title: Hold the selected id, not the event
nodes.why: An id survives the filter and a re-render, and the preview, the pressed state and the style all derive from it.
nodes.tradeoff: An object works while the list is fixed, but a refreshed list holds new objects, and an identity comparison would then select nothing.

nodes.title: Derive the visible rows from the filter
nodes.why: The visible rows are a function of the events and the text, so nothing has to be kept in step by hand.
nodes.alternative: Keep a filtered copy in state and update it on every keystroke.
nodes.tradeoff: A second copy can drift from the events, and every change to the events must remember to refilter it.

nodes.title: aria-pressed drives the selected style
nodes.why: Each row is a toggle-like button, so `aria-pressed` tells assistive technology which one is selected, and styling `[aria-pressed='true']` keeps the look in step with it.
nodes.alternative: Add an `is-selected` class and leave the attribute out.
nodes.tradeoff: A class changes only the look; screen reader users would not hear which row is selected.
